summary: This work demonstrates a cavity array microscope (CAM) with over 600 simultaneously resonant optical cavities, achieving array-averaged finesse $F = 114(17)$ and single-atom peak cooperativity $C > 10$ with 1.15 µm mode waists spaced by 10 µm, while systematically characterizing aberrations, losses, and misalignment sensitivities that limit scalability to tens of thousands of cavities. The authors identify field curvature from aspheric lenses and optical imperfections as primary constraints, provide quantitative alignment tolerances (300 nm transverse, 10 µm longitudinal for the spherical lens), and demonstrate nanometer-scale aberration characterization via interferometric degeneracy measurements.
motivation: Large neutral atom arrays require a parallelized cavity interface to achieve high-bandwidth quantum networking and fast non-destructive readout, but existing single-cavity or nanophotonic approaches suffer from limited bandwidth, small atom-surface separations, or incompatibility with large-scale atom arrays.
method: The CAM uses intra-cavity optics (microlens array, demagnifying and retro-reflecting telescopes with aspheric lenses) to create a 2D array of diffraction-limited TEM$_{00}$ modes. The authors perform paraxial and ray-traced numerical simulations to understand cavity stability and field curvature effects, measure cavity transmission spectra via a spatial light modulator, characterize degeneracy with an 80 MHz offset locking beam, and decompose detuning maps into Zernike polynomials to isolate aberration contributions.
result: With 537 cavities degenerate within the readout-optimized linewidth (5.5 MHz, finesse $F^* \approx 26$), the system achieves 53% collection efficiency—an order of magnitude above standard atom arrays—with a 140 µm field-of-view limited by aspheric field curvature (quadratic focal shift of ~2.4 nm per cavity per µm asphere displacement); projections using wide-field-of-view microscope objectives indicate feasibility of $> 10^4$ cavities with $F > 400$ and GHz-scale entanglement bandwidth.
